title: Amish Christmas Cookie Tour in Lancaster

description:

title: Ride the Pa Abandoned Turnpike 20 F
description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup
Join members and friends of the Lancaster Bicycle Club and Rails for Trails for a bike ride through the abandoned tunnels of the Pennsylvania Turnpike. When the turnpike was expanded to go over the mountain at Breezewood, three tunnels and a plaza were abandoned. The trail is 10 miles long and flat.

From Lancaster
We will meet together, leaving the parking lot of Walmart, the 222 Ephrata exit on Saturday morning, November 21st at 8am. Use Meet Up comments to make arrangements and please carpool. We will drive North one exit on 222, getting on the Turnpike and driving West to the Breezwood exit. This is a 1 and ½ hour drive. After getting off the turnpike we will meet re-group at the exit at Scheetz.
From Maryland
Drive directly to the in intersection of Rt. 30 and the Pa Turnpike exit at Breezwood. Everyone meeting at Sheetz at 10am.
The entrance to the trail is 1/2 mile away, route 30 and Tannery Road.

Caution
-since 1968 the trail has been abandoned. It is mostly gravel now.
-no road bikes…
-there are no lights in these tunnels. You must have bright front lights on you bicycles.
-one tunnel is 1 ½ mile long, completely dark.
After returning to Breezwood, we will hang out and eat together at Bob Evan’s. Each rider will wear a helmet and have a tube for you or someone to fix.
Richard Conner, leader
717-572-8480

title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour
location: Unique Lancaster, 23 N Walnut Street, Lancaster, 17603, United States
description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally! 


Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. 


Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. 


But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. 


As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. 


Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. 


Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

description:

title: Children's Chapel
location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. 
After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. 
The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. 
Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.

title: Klezmer and Jewish Music by members of Quartet Harriet: Christopher Brooks, violin and Laurie Reese, violoncello
location: Lititz, LTZ Community Room
description:
Music, Everyone

Join us for an evening of Klezmer and Jewish music. Klezmer music is traditional instrumental music of the Ashkenazi Jews. Meet the musicians; Christopher Brooks was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York. He began studying the violin at PS 8 in Brooklyn Heights and at the Third Street Music School. Attending the New School of Music in Philadelphia, Mr. Brooks studied violin with Jascha Brodsky and Geoffrey Michaels. He has played chamber music and been a member of numerous orchestras. Laurie Haines Reese is a cellist dedicated to creating and performing music—especially new music—that explores the cello’s creative possibilities. An accomplished classical musician with a lifelong curiosity about what else the cello can do, she is equally at home in folk, jazz, improvisatory, and experimental music. Based in Lancaster, PA, Laurie has freelanced and concertized extensively throughout the United States and Europe.This performance is made possible through a grant from the Yiddish Book Center. The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.

Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. Drug or RX plans are those you can switch at this time of year. You can also switch from an Advantage Plan to another Advantage Plan or to an Original Medicare Plan. The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

Wednesday Evening Prayer
Wednesdays with the Saints via Zoom Only

Yours is the day, O God, yours also the night; you established the moon and the sun. You fixed all the boundaries of the earth; you made both summer and winter. Psalm 74:15,16 

I will bless the Lord who gives me counsel; my heart teaches me, night after night. I have set the Lord always before me; because he is at my right hand, I shall not fall. Psalm 16:7,8 

Daily prayers are said on a regular schedule at Saint James. On Wednesday evenings, we invite you to explore and celebrate the inspiring lives of the saints at our Evening Prayer service. title: Dillsburg Game Night - Calvary Methodist Church in the Family Center
description:
Central PA Game Club
Dillsburg Game Night meets every Wednesday from 6:30-9:30pm for casual tabletop games. We’ve been going strong since 2016, and most Wednesdays you’ll find about 30-40 gamers who love to learn and teach new games. It’s a great group of friendly people.

Given the timeframe, most of the games played are light to medium Euros, although many of us also love card games (including trick-taking games) and party games. We have a library of about 200 games available to play, and people typically bring their own games as well.

We also run long game days (typically every other month, usually a Saturday 2-9pm) and other special events. Join us on Facebook or Discord for more information about those.

Attendees do not often RSVP on Meetup. It may show 1 person is coming but we have 40 people every Wednesday and will cancel the event if it is not happening. Feel free to message with questions.

Cost: Free
Who: All Ages (15 and under must be accompanied by an adult)
When: Every Wednesday (6:30-9:30pm)
Where: Calvary Methodist Church (Dillsburg, PA) Family Center
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/groups/2249345335100181

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

A guided tour of two of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges

—————————————————
Presented by Big Fan Presents
—————————————————
Shakedown Citi is a fresh new force on the jam band scene, born in the heart of a Grateful Dead parking lot at Citi Field in 2023.  When the band’s members crossed paths on Shakedown Street, something clicked – and the music hasn’t stopped since. 
Rather than imitating the Dead, Shakedown Citi channels their spirit – creating spontaneous, soulful performances that feel alive, adventurous and totally in the moment. Each set is a journey, full of unexpected twists, deep grooves and musical conversation that pulls even the most skeptical listener into the vibe.  Every Shakedown Citi show begins long before the first note.  Each setlist is thoughtfully and meticulously crafted from the Dead repertoire, affiliated catalogs and beyond, balancing deep cuts and beloved anthems, rarities and reprises.  No two nights are ever the same – each performance stands as a work of art on its own, alive in its moment, while also fitting into the larger patchwork of the repertoire.   
It’s not just a tribute – it’s the Dead, reborn.

—————————————————
Presented by Big Fan Presents
—————————————————
The Small Town Titans return to Mickey’s Black Box for their annual Home Town Holiday Show! 
The Small Town Titans are an American rock n’ roll power trio from York, PA who love to constantly create, as well as play live. Gone is the notion that a rock band should only release 10 songs at a time every 2 years. In a world where music fans crave new content constantly, the Small Town Titans aim to deliver their brand of art all of the time, drawing inspiration from a newer wave of rock bands such as Highly Suspect and Royal Blood, and rock legends such as the Foo Fighters, Audioslave, and Deep Purple. Thanks to their efforts at taking matters into their own hands, STT can create and release songs, podcasts, live online concerts, and more with no rules. In a social media driven world, STT knows releasing quality, constant content is as important as playing great live shows. 
In November of 2018, the band’s cover of the Christmas song “You’re a Mean One, Mr. Grinch” went viral in a matter of days, leading to charting on various Billboard charts including Holiday Digital Song Sales, Rock Digital Song Sales, Emerging Artists, and reaching #5 on the Next Big Sound chart. The song also reached #2 on the iTunes Rock charts, only being surpassed by Queen’s “Bohemian Rhapsody”. STT quickly found themselves achieving success, all on their own terms. As a continued unsigned act, all three members have risen to the occasion to continue to make music the way they want to, free from having to follow traditional music industry rules. By changing their mindset and focus towards creating content like many successful YouTubers, STT has made fans the old fashioned way, by word of mouth. 
With no manager, label, or radio support, the Small Town Titans have managed to find success by simply never forgetting one thing, their fans, both new and old. Instead of trying to make a million fans, STT is focusing on the fans they already have, and the ones they continue to make. With a love for playing live, a Small Town Titans show has evolved into more than a concert. It’s an event, with a set list that’s decided right before the show, and plenty of stage banter in between songs. The band simply hits the stage to deliver an energy driven show using guitars, drums, and their voices. Nothing more, nothing less. This approach to their live performances has led to them sharing the stage with acts such as Highly Suspect, Papa Roach, Black Stone Cherry, Pop Evil, and more. 
Check out the Small Town Titans here!

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Feeling Lucky: Mistletoe Season
location: Lucky Dog Cafe, 1942 Columbia Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
A neighborhood cafe on Columbia Avenue, the kind of easygoing local spot where there’s no dress code and no scene, just a comfortable room where people actually talk. December fills up with parties full of people you already know. This is the other kind of night: a room full of singles who showed up on purpose, a game at your table so nobody starts cold, and a Wednesday that actually goes somewhere. How the night works: You check in with a host and get a name tag. There’s nothing to download and no profile to fill out at the door. The evening runs in three movements. First, you’re seated at a small table with a game to play. That’s the icebreaker, so nobody has to invent an opening line cold, and the men move one table along each round, which means every round is a genuinely new set of people. Then the structure drops away and it’s open mingling: go where you want, talk to whoever you want, for as long as it’s working. By that point you’ve already met most of the room. Last, one-on-ones with the people you haven’t already sat with. Near the end you privately note anyone you’d like to see again, and nobody else sees it. If someone noted you back, that’s a match, and you both get it that night. $29.99 through Wednesday, November 18, then $34.99. 21+ with valid ID.

title: We the People First Friday: McCaskey Combined Choirs
location: Ware Center for the Arts, 42 N. Prince St., Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Celebrate the vibrant sound of the J.P. McCaskey High School Combined Choirs in this free concert at the Ware Center in Lancaster. The ensemble, made up of the McCaskey Vocal Ensemble and McCaskey Voices of Freedom, will present a diverse program featuring both accompanied and a cappella choral music.

To complement the evening’s art exhibit, the choirs will perform music from African culture, showcasing the students’ versatility and the range of musical styles they study throughout the school year, including both sacred and secular music.

As J.P. McCaskey High School approaches its celebration of 90 years of choral music in Lancaster, come support these talented student singers and experience an evening of music, culture, and community.

From 5 to 8 p.m., stop by the Regitz Gallery to celebrate the opening of “The Places We Go II,” a solo exhibition by Ghanaian mixed-media artist Ross Junior Owusu exploring migration as an interior and ongoing process of becoming. Through ceramics, assemblage, and mixed-media artwork, Owusu examines how memory, resilience, cultural identity, and belonging are carried, reshaped, and rebuilt across shifting landscapes.

Free and open to the public!

Free Medicare Enrollment & Benefits Class — Get Your Questions Answered!Turning 65 soon, or looking to get more out of your current health coverage? Join us for a free, informative Medicare Enrollment Class designed to help you understand your options and make confident decisions.Whether you are enrolling for the first time or looking to pair Medicare with your existing insurance to pick up extra coverage, we’ll walk you through how everything works together—and how even a baseline plan can save you big in the long run.What You’ll Learn:Eligibility & Coordination: How Medicare works for individuals 65 and older (plus qualifying exceptions) and how it coordinates alongside your current employer or private insurance.Beyond Basic Coverage: How Medicare and Medicare Advantage plans can help cover major procedures like knee replacement surgery as well as everyday essentials—including glasses, contacts, dental checkups, fillings, crowns, hearing aids, and more.Simple, Affordable Payment Options: How plan premiums can be conveniently deducted straight from your Social Security benefit or paycheck so you never have to worry about missing a bill.Special Guest Q&A with Linda: Bring your questions! Our special guest, Linda, will be on hand to answer anything on your mind—from comparing plan types to recommending coverage options tailored to your household's specific health needs and budget.Come chat with us, grab helpful resources, and get clarity on your healthcare future—at zero cost and with zero obligation!

In celebration of the centennial of Milne’s timeless tales, join Dr. Sarah Jackson, Assistant Professor from the Department of Early, Middle, and Elementary Education at Millersville University to learn about how these beloved children’s stories have endured as they have been translated and adapted countless times since their publication 100 years ago. Dr. Jackson will focus on the influence of colonialism in the stories and consider how the animal characters try on—and resist—colonial language. All ages welcome, but this will be a lecture-style program geared toward the young at heart 😉Registration is helpful, but walk-ins will not be turned away.

title: Monthly Club Meeting - "Wearables for Wildlife: Behind the Scenes with the Evolution of Wildlife Telemetry Technologies"
location: North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 
Presented by Club President Andy McGann 
Andy McGann grew up birding in Southcentral Pennsylvania and his early experiences ultimately led to a career in the field of Movement Ecology. His time in academia, non-profits, consulting, and ultimately to a wildlife telemetry tech company spanned a timeframe that saw the science advance from analog radio telemetry to “smart devices” with GPS, accelerometers, and global Internet connectivity. In his career, Andy combined his experiences in ornithology with his love of technology and appreciation for geography in order to help wildlife researchers and organizations around the world obtain the scientific information needed to help conserve some of the rarest birds we have left. Andy will discuss the evolution of the technology, the current state-of-the-art, and paint a picture of where we are going.

title: Geminids Meteor Shower at Millport Conservancy
location: Millport Conservancy, 737 E. Millport Rd., Lititz, PA, 17543, United States
description:
[vc_row][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”128240″] 
Geminids are the most active meteor shower of the year!
Join us at Millport Conservancy on the night of Sunday, December 13th, to observe what could be the most spectacular meteor shower of the year! Far from the city lights of Lancaster, the darker skies of Millport mean we could see up to 30+ meteors, if the weather cooperates! 
The Geminids are the most active meteor shower of the year, and are considered one of the two best showers for viewing (along with August’s Perseids). The Geminids are unlike most other meteor showers, in that they are not likely caused by a debris field from a comet. Instead, the Geminids have been identified as being spawned from the debris field of 3200 Phaethon, which is what seems to be an asteroid. Astronomers believe Phaethon is an asteroid because it lacks the trail of a typical comet when it passes the Sun, and its spectra looks like that of a rocky asteroid. Additionally, the debris left behind by Phaethon is denser than that of a typical comet. 
However, the object does have a highly elliptical, or non-circular/”stretched out”, orbit, which is atypical for an asteroid but common for comets. Phaethon’s strange orbit gives astronomers pause when labeling it as “just” an asteroid, and some astronomers have proposed that Phaethon may actually be a “dead comet”, or even possibly an entirely new type of object that some astronomers are starting to call a “rock comet”. 
Whatever Phaethon is, the debris field it has left has made for great views here on Earth! Every year, around December 13th and 14th, the Earth passes through the debris field. When this happens, the Earth can be thought of as pushing through the debris, made up of tiny rocks, and pulling them into our atmosphere with the help of gravity. All the rocks burning up in our atmosphere is what can be seen as the meteor shower we all know and love. 
Keep an eye out in the coming weeks for more information about the North Museum’s Geminids Star Party, as well as general observing tips and information about the meteor shower![/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)
source: Meetup: The Creative House of Lancaster

title: Swoon Squad: A Romance TBR Book Club
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center A
description:
Book Club, Adults, Seniors

Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! The Discussion: We gather to swap recommendations, vent about our favorite (and least favorite) clichés, and discover new authors through each other's picks.Come ready to share your pick, discuss the tropes, and meet fellow romance fans in a comfortable library setting ❤️June 29 - ⚔️Enemies to Lovers ⚔️July 27 - 🥰😠Grumpy/Sunshine😠🥰August 31 - 🏆Sports Romance🏆September 28 - 📖Academic Romance📖October 26 - 🧛Paranormal Romance🧛November 30 - 🛏️Forced Proximity🛏️December 28 - 🎁Holiday Romance🎁

title: Being One Online Spiritual Support Group
description:
Being One Center in Lancaster County
Life can be frustrating and distressing!
Sometimes we just feel overwhelmed, insecure, or lost!

The good news is, you're not alone!

We warmly invite you to check-in and connect with community in our Online Spiritual Support Group. In each meeting, we will discuss our current stressors and see how we can positively cope using our spiritual tools to overcome these challenges.

Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.

Donations Greatly Appreciated!

This Event is lovingly hosted By Anna Bojczuk. Anna is a Registered nurse with over 40 years of experience as well as a gifted Energy worker. Anna is also long-time volunteer and inspiration in the Being One Center Community.

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

title: Swoon Squad: A Romance TBR Book Club

description:

Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! There is no fee to attend our meetings which range from topical subjects of interest to freethinkers such as Church/State Separation, as well as subjects such as science, philosophy, ethics, counter-apologetics, and psychology. All are welcome to attend no matter what your beliefs may be but proselytizing is not allowed. Bring your articles, news, jokes, gripes, questions, ideas, topics, or anything else you would like to discuss with the rest of the group.

Hope to see you there!

description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

If you would like a second slot, you can get on the waitlist by telling Miss Esther. If there are spots left, it will be first come first serve.If you can't make it after registering, please contact Miss Esther at emartin@manheimlibrary.org or call (717)665-6700 Ext. 4200 for the circulation desk so we can take you off the list and allow everyone a chance.When you arrive, you will need a book to read. You have the library at your disposal or you can bring your own. You can start halfway if you want. Read whatever you like!

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Lancaster Scrapbooking & Papercrafting Monthly gathering
description:
Lancaster Scrapbooking, Cards & Papercrafts
Scrapbook, make cards, practice quilling, or paint!
Meeting on the third Tuesday, 6-10 p.m., at the Cozy Crop House. (Also meeting the next night, Wednesday, same time & place. You can come to one or both, and can leave your gear overnight.) A chance to meet & gather monthly with local scrapbookers & crafters, in an ideal crafting environment! Plenty of room to do your own thing while we socialize. Bring your own supplies & projects, or just sit back and relax with scrapping friends, and watch & learn a new technique.
Specific crafting events (eg. card classes, paint nights, etc) may be featured here as scheduled.
Bring snacks to share if you wish.
Meetup groups are charged a monthly administration fee which is currently paid in this group by a few members. VOLUNTARY donations of $1 or $2 into a group "kitty" will help us continue the group's open membership and online advertising. The rate it costs our _whole group_ is about $12/month for a 6-month commitment. Please do not feel you cannot come if you don't contribute--the fee is paid, and donations are voluntary to cover future fees.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)
source: Meetup: The Creative House of Lancaster

title: Night Shift at Lancaster Science Factory
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Night Shift 2026-27  
Overview: Experience the Lancaster Science Factory in a whole new way when you stay overnight! Explore over 75 hands-on exhibits, enjoy a pre-lights-out snack, unroll your sleeping bag in the exhibit hall, and have a light breakfast before you leave in the morning. New to this year, educators will be leading hands-on STEM workshops in our Maker Space! Consider joining us for the Night Shift with your scout group, sports team or even for a special birthday!  
Tickets: Tickets for the Night Shift are just $65 and include activity guides, a hands-on STEM workshop, snacks, and breakfast. This program is limited to children ages 6-12 and one adult (18+) is required for every three children. No adults will be admitted without children.   
Dates:  
Saturday, November 7-Sunday, November 8, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, December 5-Sunday, December 6, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, February 13-Sunday, February 14, 2027  

Click here to register 

Saturday, April 17-Sunday, April 18, 2027  

Click here to register 

Itinerary:  

6:30-7:00 pm: Arrival, check in 


7:00-10:00 pm: Museum exploration, Science Cafe activity, scavenger hunts, workshops 


7:15-7:55: Group A workshop 


8:05-8:45: Group B workshop 


8:55-9:25: Group C workshop 


10:00-10:30 pm: Set up sleeping accommodations 


10:30 pm: Get ready for lights out 


7:00-8:00 am: Light breakfast available 


8:30 am: Exhibit hall closes 

Questions? Reach out to mstoltzfus@tlsf.org

title: Lancaster Scrapbooking & Papercrafting Monthly gathering
description:
Lancaster Scrapbooking, Cards & Papercrafts
Scrapbook, make cards, practice quilling, or paint!
Meeting on the third Tuesday, 6-10 p.m., at the Cozy Crop House. (Also meeting the next night, Wednesday, same time & place. You can come to one or both, and can leave your gear overnight.) A chance to meet & gather monthly with local scrapbookers & crafters, in an ideal crafting environment! Plenty of room to do your own thing while we socialize. Bring your own supplies & projects, or just sit back and relax with scrapping friends, and watch & learn a new technique.
Specific crafting events (eg. card classes, paint nights, etc) may be featured here as scheduled.
Bring snacks to share if you wish.
Meetup groups are charged a monthly administration fee which is currently paid in this group by a few members. VOLUNTARY donations of $1 or $2 into a group "kitty" will help us continue the group's open membership and online advertising. The rate it costs our _whole group_ is about $12/month for a 6-month commitment. Please do not feel you cannot come if you don't contribute--the fee is paid, and donations are voluntary to cover future fees.
